speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Recently, many Members of this House had participated in the 25 push-ups a day challenge, raising awareness for mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Some members of the public had asked what is the point of all these?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When we come together to go beyond the label to lay the foundation to eradicate mental health stigmatisations.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I recall about 20 years ago, as a young Rota commander at a fire station attending to my first suicide incident.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When I checked the call sheet, it was on the 13th floor, cliché.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As I went into the unit, I saw the subject standing close to the window and I was told that I had a few minutes before the rescue set-up would be complete.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I engaged in small talk with the subject in the hope to distract him from our elaborate rescue set-up.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Out of respect, I shall not share the outcome but I must say that the episode left a deep impression on me.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It made me curious about mental resilience and the importance of a sound support systems that include family, friends and peers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In my role as an educator, and as a community leader, one persistent issue that I have been confronted time and again is with regards to mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Periodically, I receive news of suicide within the community and every single time, news of an individual taking his or her life hits me hard.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If we picture a pyramid structure of mental health issues, usually suicide is at the peak.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What I want to bring forth today is not the peak, but the myriad of ways individuals in our community may be affected with mental health issues and how we may remove the stigmatisation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: That means there is a high chance that someone you know, may know someone else who has suffered a mental health issue.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The fact that we do not know any, may suggest that: (a) we do not know, really; (b) we do not know; or worse; (c) we deny knowing people who know; because of the stigmatisation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is common for us to label people with mental health issues as highly emotional, mentally weak, crazy, or even naturally violent, and we stay away from them.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, it is clear that having awareness is important.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe that it is important to make mental health literacy programmes mandatory in our schools and institutes of higher learning or IHLs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In that way, our students are not only able to identify such symptoms in themselves, or their friends, but they now can take an additional step to address such symptoms.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: These programmes may include self-care and of course, stress management.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, rather than artificially creating a peer support programme in schools and IHLs led by student leaders, or handing the responsibility to teachers, lecturers or even the counsellors, we have an organic one where friends look out for one another because now they know they have the knowledge and they can help.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Like how we offer first-aid classes for our students and there is a first-aid kit, we may now need to develop a mental health first-aid kit.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We can also replicate this at our workplaces.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And I am sure the MOM got that covered in their upcoming advisory guide, and if not, I hope they will include it in the upcoming advisory.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the years, there have been discussions on the relationship between social media and mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I embarked in a systematic review of this relationship, and I was surprised to find that many studies actually shared that social media has a net neutral effect – that means the positives and the negatives cancel out each other.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The reason for this is that it creates a platform for people to share and raise awareness.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In the hands of the knowledgeable and in the hands of the discerning, it is an important social tool.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, one clear negative effect of social media is cyberbullying and the creation of fake realities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This effect is not only observed in children or youths, but also adults.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I suppose it would be far-fetched for me to suggest that we legislate against cyberbullying, or the creation of fake realities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, I do think it is feasible for us to roll out a digital literacy programme for our children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Through this, I hope the future generations of social media users are discerning and are able to uphold an unwritten code of conduct.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In my conversation with mental health patients, many highlighted the need for greater accessibility, both in terms of quantity and in terms of the ease of getting support, especially for those at the early stage.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Imagine, you are feeling depressed, with a heavy head, heavy feet and walking into a psychiatric ward in a hospital and compare that with walking into a GP clinic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Help-seeking touchpoints must be community based and non-labelling.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This will not only encourage those who suspect they have mental health issues to come forward to seek help but it also lowers the stigmatisation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Inadvertently, this will create a new norm whereby it is okay to seek help if you feel unwell, or unmotivated, or are just feeling plain lousy.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mental health issues are like other illnesses, if treated early, there is high chance of a speedy recovery.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thus, the Community Mental Health Programme by MOH must continue to expand.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This involves having screening mechanisms in place in primary care settings like the GP clinics I mentioned earlier, or paediatric clinics, or gynaecological clinics, in schools and in IHLs, and also in the workplace.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Anyone screened for being at risk or having symptoms of mental health issues, would be referred promptly to a clinic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The objective is to get people engaged early, before the illness has effects on the brain, disrupts their lives and risks them doing something that would harm themselves or others.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Like in some sports where time-outs are allowed, it allows the team to re-strategise, to reorganise and recharge as they continue on with the game.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Similarly, I hope such time-outs could be introduced in schools and workplaces.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A student or is having a really hard time in school.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He or she feels overwhelmed, overworked and is falling behind, and they know, they know they need help.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: All he or she has to do now is to inform his or her parents, and the parents will call the school to ask for an excuse for the absence.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, it is not really a free pass for these students.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Most importantly, the parents are now aware and the school has their absence recorded as a mental day so that they can keep track on how many the student has taken.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If the student takes a second one, the student would be referred to the school counsellor for a quick chat.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This is important because we can catch students who are struggling before it is too late.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Rather than waiting for the results to dip in mid semester, or worse, at the end of the semester, we can now intervene much earlier.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: At the same time, we are creating a culture that it is okay.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is okay if you need to take a break because mental health is just as important as physical health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I have had students who struggled midway, took a break, and came back stronger with much improved grades.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Another form of time-out that I strongly believe in but will not elaborate further is the Right to Disconnect legislature as raised by the hon Member, Mr Melvin Yong.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He had discussed this at length yesterday and I am in support of this.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Just like him, I await the good news from MOM.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He lived with depression for about 12 years.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He even went through the Singapore Armed Forces’ Officer Cadet School with this depression.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He experienced suicidal tendencies and thoughts in 2011 but before he could continue with his attempt, he had a simple text on the phone asking how he was doing in school.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: That led him to seek help and he overcame his depression in 2017.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Nicholas has created the Ekho Academy, an online learning portal to provide support, share tips and stories of hope and recovery.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: She was diagnosed with schizophrenia and depression when she was 19 while in university.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Her mother noticed that she was not feeling well, took her to a GP, and subsequently she received treatment at a hospital.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: She took some time-off, but when she came back, she managed to graduate with a second-class honours in Social Sciences.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Sumaiyah is now married and a mother to a beautiful daughter.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: He started experiencing hallucinations and feelings of paranoia when he was only 18 years old.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But he was lucky because he was able to seek help and was diagnosed with schizophrenia and depression early.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Desmond is currently in recovery and is using his personal experience to inspire other youths and those struggling with schizophrenia.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Collectively, they have proven to me the importance of intervention checkpoints and how they are able to move on with their lives and continue to achieve success.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   In my speech earlier, I highlighted the issue of mental health in our society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In every life journey, each individual will certainly face challenges and obstacles and experience stress.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In every phase and area of life, be it in schools, workplaces or homes and in domestic affairs, all of us will face pressure from time to time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Sadly, there are many within our community who belittle mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is easy for us to label someone with mental health issues as being too emotional, weak in their faith or that they are crazy and so on.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We must build an open-minded society and provide support to individuals facing mental challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We should consider mental illness just like physical illness and provide the same professional treatment.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: If one needs further help, I suggest that they seek professional mental treatment, such as therapy and so on.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us together become a society that is more caring and ready to help those who are facing mental health challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, we live in a highly dynamic world, a complex and interconnected world, a world where cuts and bruises may be inflicted covertly and hidden from our family and friends to see, a world where non linearity exists – small changes may lead to large implications and big changes may sometimes lead to small implications.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A clear example would be the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It has shown how interconnected we are and how dynamic the situation can change.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I look forward to the New Joint Task Force and would like to put forth my name to be included in the task force in the future.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: There is a relevant quote summarising my speech today by Alexander Den Heijer who said, "When a flower does not bloom, you fix the environment in which it grows, not the flower".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have about three minutes if anyone wants to chime in before the response.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I thank Members of the House for your patience for the next 10 minutes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Rest assured I have your mental well-being at heart.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our work ahead of us can be categorised into two broad categories: first, fighting stigma; second, to lend better support for mental wellness in general and for individuals with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Before we look ahead let us first take stock of what already has been done.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since 2018, NCSS has passionately powered Beyond the Label movement, a campaign that aims at amplifying the anti-stigma message.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: NCSS has worked with partners to develop resources, organise outreach activities and the annual Beyond the Label Festival, which allows the general public to have a better understanding of the stigma faced by persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond broad-based campaigns, work has also been done in a more targeted fashion.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, MOE has incorporated the learning of socio-emotional skills and resilience building into school curriculum, CCAs and other programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We recognise the importance of equipping our children with the socio-emotional skills to handle challenges and better bounce back from difficult situations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is all the more important in a world that is currently struggling with COVID-19 and its aftermath.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Next year, MOE will introduce the enhanced Character and Citizenship Education or CCE featuring mental health education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It will include topics such as "understanding common mental health issues and symptoms" and "developing empathy towards people struggling with mental health conditions".

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the other hand, HPB has also been conducting mental well-being roadshows and workshops at our workplaces.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From next month, HPB will be rolling out the Peer Support @ Work series to help employees better understand how and what it means to be a peer supporter at work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also invited persons living with mental health conditions to serve as ambassadors in our anti-stigma movement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since 2016, the Peer Support Specialist programme led by NCSS has been equipping persons with mental health conditions to leverage their lived experiences to inspire, empower and support others in their recovery journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, lending better support for mental well-being generally, as well as for persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Within our communities, MOH and AIC has established community outreach and intervention teams, started mental health and dementia services in polyclinics, and trained GP partners to diagnose and support persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To cushion the impact of COVID-19 on mental well-being in our communities, MSF – with MOH's support – set up the National CARE Hotline in April this year to provide emotional and psychological support to those in distress.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Cases needing specialised support beyond what the helpline could offer are referred to service providers such as the IMH, the Samaritans of Singapore or SOS and other social service agencies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To help someone who needs to navigate through available resources on mental health, the MOH Office for Healthcare Transformation, MSF, NCSS and IMH launched mindline.sg in July this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mindline.sg is a portal offering resources on mental health, including a standardised tool for users to assess their own emotional well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Not forgetting Belle, the Beyond the Label chatbot that connects users to a comprehensive list of mental health services and resources based on keywords.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In essence, we have covered some ground in eradicating stigma, channelling resource to the mental wellness landscape and supporting individuals with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But, make no mistake: we remain a "work in progress" and our approach needs to evolve.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To that end, I am heartened to share that since February this year, the open call to recruit those keen to contribute to the Youth Mental Well-being Network saw over 1,000 youths, parents, care-givers, mental health practitioners and professionals pitching in.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Network takes a ground-up approach, with members surfacing ideas and identifying the areas they want to work on.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It takes the view that Government does not have a monopoly of ideas, but we want to journey with the community in co-creating solutions in the spirit of SG Together.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since work in the Network started, members have stepped forward to lead discussions, developed ideas and initiatives to strengthen support for our youth's mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Alongside the Network, the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce has been more recently convened to provide a coordinated national response to the mental health needs of Singaporeans arising from the pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Taskforce is co-led by MOH and the Institute of Mental Health, with members from MOM, MOE, MSF, MCCY, HPB, AIC, NCSS and PA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because we recognise that the issue of mental wellness and mental health has many facades.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Members of the multi-disciplinary Taskforce can leverage their colleagues' areas of expertise in staging a holistic response to address mental health issues arising from COVID-19 and beyond.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Once again, I thank the hon Member for spotlighting mental wellness and mental health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is an issue that we, as a society need to continually work on.
